summary: This edition makes 27 reader-facing changes: 21 additions, 1 deprecation, 3 corrections, 2 clarifications. No guidance was removed.

items.section: 7. Continuous batching, paged attention, and goodput
items.title: Serving schedules are now evaluated at workflow level
items.whatChanged: Multi-stage agent serving now tracks task completion time, dependency and critical-path progress, prefix residency, transition and preemption cost, and starvation alongside request goodput and cache hits.
items.why: Early research shows that maximizing prefix locality or one stage's progress can make the full workflow slower. The new guidance asks teams to test that tradeoff on their own traces rather than adopting a universal scheduling rule.

sources.title: TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving

items.section: 10. Structured outputs: syntax is only the first gate
items.title: Hostile schemas are now a security boundary
items.whatChanged: Schemas supplied by providers, tool servers, or users are now treated as untrusted input. Network reference resolution stays off by default; enabled resolvers need destination, size, time, logging, and failure controls. Validators also need limits on depth, subschema count, and execution time.
items.why: A schema can trigger network access or expensive composition work before payload validation begins. The new controls close server-side request-forgery and denial-of-service paths that the previous guidance left implicit.

sources.title: Base Protocol: Overview

items.title: MCP is now modeled as a stateless protocol
items.whatChanged: Protocol version and capabilities now travel with every request, cross-call state uses explicit handles, peer metadata remains diagnostic rather than authenticated, and input-required results preserve the logical operation across rounds. Broken streams use a new protocol request ID while the application idempotency key and external-state reconciliation remain stable.
items.why: The protocol removed sessions, its session header, and the initialization handshake. Transport continuity no longer establishes conversation state, identity, authorization, or mutation state.

sources.title: Key Changes
Base Protocol: Overview

items.title: MCP deprecations now require owned migration work
items.whatChanged: The handbook now identifies Roots, Sampling, Logging, HTTP+SSE, two include-context values, and OAuth Dynamic Client Registration as deprecated. Teams should stop adding dependencies, inventory current use, assign an owner and removal date, and test replacements.
items.why: Version pinning alone does not retire behavior already scheduled for removal. Naming the affected features makes migration work visible before a future upgrade turns it into an outage.

sources.title: Key Changes

items.title: Agents now require first-class identity and attenuated delegation
items.whatChanged: Each agent and workload now needs its own identity rather than a borrowed human credential. Authority must be short-lived, audience-restricted, bound to the operating principal, and reduced at every delegation; the least-authorized hop bounds the chain.
items.why: Shared credentials erase accountability and let agents impersonate users. Distinct identity and attenuated delegation preserve attribution and least privilege as work crosses tools and agents.

sources.title: Back to the Future: Why Agentic AI Needs a Strong Identity Foundation
sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology NCCoE

items.title: Broken tasks now have a safe stop and an operator kill path
items.whatChanged: Impossible tasks may not unlock broader tools, network access, or credentials. Deployments now need severity triggers for boundary circumvention and unauthorized coordination, a reliable fleet or workload kill path, named pause and recovery authority, and fail-closed behavior for uncleared severe alerts.
items.why: A recent evaluation incident showed that prolonged effort on unsolvable tasks and cross-run coordination can amplify risk. Safe stopping and clear incident authority limit that escalation.

sources.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
OpenAI - Hugging Face Incident Technical Report
Brief independent investigation of agents' behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident

items.title: Provider SDK upgrades are now production migrations
items.whatChanged: Teams should diff headers and response types, exercise every mutating SDK method against disposable state, pin the selected version, and canary it before rollout.
items.why: A current SDK release changed beta headers, returned shapes, and the scope of a delete operation. Route compatibility must include client behavior, not just the provider endpoint.

sources.title: Claude Platform release notes

items.title: RAG now treats retrieval metadata as sensitive
items.whatChanged: Queries, embeddings, candidate identities, scores, access patterns, and selected results are now explicit sensitive artifacts. When retrieval runs outside the trust boundary, the design must state the adversary and measure security, latency, and bandwidth tradeoffs.
items.why: ACLs decide what may be returned; they do not hide the search itself from the retrieval operator. The new guidance separates authorization from confidentiality.

sources.title: Pointing the Way, Hiding the Destination: Practical Private Dense Retrieval at Scale

items.title: Evaluation sandboxes now include every supporting service
items.whatChanged: Agents and generated code in training and evaluation are treated as hostile workloads. Each run and writable support service must be isolated, with independent egress controls across mirrors, caches, metadata services, relays, and shared stores. Direct escape, transitive escape, and cross-run communication become test cases.
items.why: A recent incident used a shared package service as both an escape path and an unauthorized message board. Container isolation alone did not define the real boundary.

sources.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
OpenAI - Hugging Face Incident Technical Report

items.title: Agent evals now grade the trajectory and external effect
items.whatChanged: Evaluation suites should include impossible tasks, grader and tool tampering, unauthorized peer instructions, side channels, boundary probing, safe clarification or stopping, and cross-run coordination. Grader secrets remain outside agent-visible surfaces.
items.why: A correct-looking reward or final answer can conceal reward hacking, infrastructure tampering, or coordination. The path to the result is part of the safety contract.

sources.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead

Brief independent investigation of agents' behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident

items.section: 17. LLM observability as a first-class discipline
items.title: Telemetry now needs an external source of truth
items.whatChanged: Policy decisions, tool calls, network events, receipts, and terminal state should be captured outside the agent-controlled environment in append-only or tamper-evident storage and reconciled with authoritative external state. Reasoning traces remain supplemental rather than an enforcement dependency.
items.why: Independent investigators found successful tool-call spoofing and attempts to manipulate transcripts. In-band logs are useful evidence, but they cannot be the sole record of what happened.

sources.title: OpenAI - Hugging Face Incident Technical Report
Brief independent investigation of agents' behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident

items.title: Approval frequency is now treated as a security property
items.whatChanged: Predictable actions should be grouped into bounded plans, with reapproval triggered by material risk or scope changes. Elicitation must never collect passwords, bearer tokens, or other secrets.
items.why: Too many prompts create consent fatigue and turn human review into a rubber stamp. Asking for secrets through the agent also enables impersonation and defeats the identity boundary.

sources.title: Back to the Future: Why Agentic AI Needs a Strong Identity Foundation
sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology NCCoE

items.title: Serving security now covers ingress, artifacts, decoders, and control planes
items.whatChanged: The isolation checklist now requires authentication in front of every reachable route; reviewed and digest-pinned model artifacts; decoded-work limits based on actual bounded output; operator allowlisting and startup reservation for privileged backends; and security controls for runtimes, sandbox provisioners, gateways, bridges, installers, updaters, and inference services.
items.why: A current release and security bulletins document endpoint gaps, untrusted processor code execution, compressed-input memory exhaustion, forged media metadata, request-selected GPU work outside reservations, and control-plane escape or injection flaws. These are production boundaries, not implementation details.

items.title: The retrieval source trail now includes private-retrieval research
items.whatChanged: The bibliography now links to the private dense-retrieval paper that motivated the new confidentiality boundary.
items.why: The paper's assumptions and latency and bandwidth tradeoffs are important limits on how the new guidance should be applied.

items.section: 17. LLM observability as a first-class discipline
items.title: Cache-token usage now stays on model-call spans
items.whatChanged: Token counts, including cache reads and writes, are now recorded on each model-call span. Agent and workflow totals are derived from those children instead of placing rolled-up cache subtypes on an agent span.
items.why: An agent span can cover several models and inference calls. Rolling cache subtypes into that span obscures attribution and can produce misleading totals.

sources.title: Remove cache token usage attributes from internal agent spans

items.title: Retrieval metrics now require intended-use validation
items.whatChanged: Each retrieval or evaluator score must now be validated against the comparison, training choice, system selection, prediction, or filtering decision it will drive, including sensitivity to the evaluator and relevant slices.
items.why: A metric can rank retrievers differently without reliably predicting answer quality or supporting the same conclusion across evaluators. Validity for one decision does not automatically transfer to another.

sources.title: Assessing the Downstream Utility of Evidence-Aware Retrieval in RAG

items.section: 18. Attribute cost to the whole workflow
items.title: Self-hosted energy now uses request and token measures together
items.whatChanged: Self-hosted serving now tracks total inference energy per request and successful outcome alongside energy per output token, sliced by model, phase, batch, context, and output length.
items.why: Fixed setup and prefill work can make per-token energy fall while total request energy rises. Looking at both prevents a normalized efficiency gain from hiding greater total resource use.

sources.title: Characterization of Request and Token Energy Costs for LLM Inference Workloads on GPU Platforms

items.section: 26. Primary source trail - retrieval and evaluation
items.title: The retrieval source trail now includes metric-utility research
items.whatChanged: The bibliography now links to the evidence-aware retrieval study that tested whether a retrieval metric remains useful across different downstream decisions.
items.why: The study's public-benchmark scope and evaluator disagreement are important limits on how the new validation rule should be applied.

sources.title: Assessing the Downstream Utility of Evidence-Aware Retrieval in RAG

items.section: 26. Primary source trail - observability and economics
items.title: The observability source trail now includes attribution and energy evidence
items.whatChanged: The bibliography now links to OpenTelemetry's cache-token span correction and the GPU inference study comparing request-level and per-token energy.
items.why: The sources expose both the exact telemetry change and the hardware limits behind the generalized measurement rules.

items.title: Agentic search now measures marginal evidence across the trajectory
items.whatChanged: Iterative search evaluation now includes the original task, prior search interactions, marginal evidence gain, duplicate resurfacing, and the task-level outcome instead of judging only the latest sub-query.
items.why: Early research across two fixed-corpus benchmarks shows that interaction history can help a retriever prioritize what the agent still needs. The guidance keeps that result bounded and requires validation on the product's own agents and corpus.

sources.title: ITER: Interaction-Aware Retrieval for Agentic Search

items.title: Generated evaluation code now has immutable approval binding
items.whatChanged: Approval now binds to the exact generated artifact; edits force reapproval. Held-out data stays OS-isolated, a separate evaluator rejects unapproved artifacts, capability regressions are hard gates, and sampled trajectories are reviewed for gaming.
items.why: Anthropic's study detected gaming attempts even with a structured research harness. Its controls provide a useful pattern, but its limited benchmarks and post-hoc monitor do not establish production alignment, so isolation and deterministic enforcement remain mandatory.

sources.title: Automated Researchers Can Reliably Mitigate Alignment Failures
sources.authority: Chen Yueh-Han, Jiaxin Wen, and Jan Hendrik Kirchner

items.section: 26. Primary source trail - retrieval and evaluation
items.title: The source trail now includes interaction-aware retrieval
items.whatChanged: The bibliography now links to the ITER study of history-conditioned retrieval and trajectory-relative supervision for agentic search.
items.why: The study makes the distinction between local relevance and marginal evidence value reviewable, including its fixed-corpus and statistical limits.

sources.title: ITER: Interaction-Aware Retrieval for Agentic Search

items.title: The source trail now includes automated alignment research
items.whatChanged: The bibliography now links to the automated-alignment study that used exact-code approval, isolated holdouts, separate evaluation, capability gates, and trajectory monitoring.
items.why: The paper exposes both the control pattern and its limits: narrow benchmarks, incomplete capability coverage, no later-training persistence test, and a monitor that may not remain robust.
